newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-HOME-GROWN ACES RAUL AND CAMINERO LEAD DERBY SIDES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-HOME-GROWN ACES RAUL AND CAMINERO LEAD DERBY SIDES.

text.p: The best home-grown players in the cosmopolitan Spanish league meet in Saturday's Madrid derby as Real's teenage sensation Raul Gonzalez takes on Jose Luis Caminero of neighbours Atletico.
Curiously the two could easily have formed a midfield pair at club as well as international level but have ended up changing sides in a bizarre twist of fate.
Caminero began life at Real but found his way to a first-team place blocked by right-sided midfielder Michel, a player he resembles in many ways.
Caminero spent four seasons at Valladolid before joining Atletico in 1993. But he was still an unknown before he shot to prominence in the 1994 World Cup in the United States.

Atletico's league and Cup double last year owed a lot to Caminero but the 55-match season left him drained and Spanish manager Javier Clemente was forced to look elsewhere for inspiration in the Euro 96 tournament.
Caminero also shocked Atletico fans by saying he was ready to move to a 'bigger and better club' and stopped talking to the media amid rumours of personal problems.

Outspoken club president Jesus Gil has since moved to patch up the relationship and must have been proud of the midfielder when Caminero broke a six-month media silence -- to blast reporters for not paying enough attention to Atletico.
Caminero has also reappeared with a vengeance on the field.

Atletico's poor start had coincided with a series of injuries to their influential playmaker but Caminero's return to action has produced a rapid turn-around and victory on Saturday would put Radomir Antic's side right back in the championship picture.
However, Caminero's performances against Real have been forgettable to say the least.
He has missed three of the six league clashes since moving to the Vicente Calderon stadium and he was sent off for a stupid foul in last season's game at Real's Santiago Bernabeu ground.
Raul Gonzalez, on the other hand, must have good memories of lining up against Atletico.

Raul made his home debut for Real, aged just 17, against his old club and showed his class by knocking home a superb ball from Michael Laudrup, the Danish midfielder often seen as his footballing mentor.
The Spanish press went to town on the arrival of a player who had only left Atletico after Gil cut the club's junior teams as a cost-saving measure.
The same commentators were quickly demanding that coach Clemente blood the youngster at full international level.
Characteristically, Clemente waited until Raul had won praise from all over Europe for his Champions' League performances to give him his first cap.
The Italian media even dubbed the side 'Raul Madrid'.
Now 19, Raul continues to score goals despite being moved back from the forward line after the arrival of strikers Predrag Mijatovic and Davor Suker.
Coach Fabio Capello had hoped to keep his young star fresh for Saturday's game.

But his hand was forced as Valladolid put Real under heavy pressure in Wednesday's Cup tie. And it was Raul, predictably, who got Capello out of trouble by coming on as substitute to set up Mijatovic for the first, before scoring the second himself.
